question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It was in this spirit that my little ones crept about me the other evening to hear about their great-grandmother Field, who lived in a great house in Norfolk (a hundred times bigger than that in which they and papa lived), which had been the scene-so at least it was generally believed in that part of the country-of the tragic incidents wh
solution:
The correct answer is **option 2 i.e. CADB.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• While arranging the part of the sentence given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them.
 
• When we read the sentence carefully option A, option B and option D are not the starting sentence, so the starting sentence is Option C.
 
• The description of option A is in option D and the final sentence is option B, so the correct sequence of the para jumbled is **option** **2** i.e. **CADB.**

Correct answer is: **(C) **Children love to listen to stories about their elders when they were children; to stretch their imagination to the conception of a traditionary great uncle, or grandame, whom they never saw. **(A) **It was in the spirit that .... **(D) **Certain it is, that the whole story.... **(B) **Here, Alice put out one of her dear mother's look, too tender to be called upbraiding.
